what_its_for: Edaravone is used to treat amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), also known as Lou Gehrig's disease. It is a free radical scavenger that helps slow down the worsening of ALS symptoms by protecting nerve cells from damage caused by oxidative stress.
how_to_take: Edaravone comes in two forms: an intravenous (IV) infusion given by a healthcare provider, and an oral suspension (liquid) called Radicava ORS that you swallow. For the oral liquid form, shake the bottle well before each use and measure the dose carefully with the dosing syringe provided. You can take it with or without food. Do not mix it with other liquids. Swallow it directly or place it in your mouth using the syringe.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. The typical adult dosing schedule follows cycles: during the first treatment cycle, you receive a dose every day for 14 days in a row, followed by a 14-day break (no medication). For all cycles after the first one, you receive a dose for 10 out of 14 days, then take a 14-day break. Each cycle lasts 28 days total. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it or receive it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. Call your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store the oral liquid (Radicava ORS) at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from light and do not refrigerate or freeze it. Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep all forms of edaravone out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor about all medications, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting edaravone, as it may interact with other drugs. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or unwell after taking this medication. Do not stop taking edaravone without talking to your doctor first. Avoid exposing the medication to extreme heat or cold.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience: signs of a serious allergic reaction such as hives, itching, rash, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, trouble breathing, or feel faint; trouble breathing or shortness of breath; chest tightness; severe dizziness; or any unusual swelling. Also contact your doctor if you notice any new or worsening symptoms, if you have kidney problems, or if you develop a sulfite allergy reaction (the oral form contains sodium bisulfite).
when_it_works: Edaravone does not cure ALS, but it may help slow the decline in your ability to function physically. Some patients may begin to notice stabilization of their condition within the first few treatment cycles, but results vary from person to person. It is important to continue taking the medication as prescribed and keep all follow-up appointments with your doctor to monitor how well the treatment is working for you.
special_populations: Patients with asthma or sulfite allergies should use extra caution with the oral form (Radicava ORS) because it contains sodium bisulfite, which can cause serious allergic reactions. There is limited information on the safety of edaravone during pregnancy or breastfeeding; talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety and effectiveness in children have not been established. Older adults and patients with kidney or liver problems should be closely monitored by their doctor while using this medication.
